content.text: Discover dates, groups, qualifying format and the number of places up for grabs at the FIFA World Cup 26.UEFA FIFA World Cup 26 qualifying began in March 2025Sixteen spots at global showpiece on offer View key information about the groups and how qualification worksFIFA World Cup 26™ tickets: 16FIFA World Cup 26™ tickets: 16DatesDatesEurope's World Cup 26 qualifying competition began in March 2025 and will conclude in March 2026.Draw and groupsDraw and groupsThe UEFA Preliminary Draw took place on Friday, 13 December 2024, with the 54 competing nations drawn into 12 groups.All of the 12 sections are now confirmed after March’s UEFA Nations League (UNL) quarter-finals, with Germany (Group A), France (Group D), Spain (Group E) and Portugal (Group F) overcoming Italy (Group I), Croatia (Group L), Netherlands (Group G) and Denmark (Group C), respectively.FIFA World Cup 26™: UEFA preliminary round final standingsFIFA World Cup 26™: UEFA preliminary round final standingsFIFA World Cup™ UEFA Qualifiers - Türkiye tackle Romania and Slovakia face Kosovo in Path C, with Denmark meeting North Macedonia in Path D, where Czechia are up against Republic of Ireland.How qualifying worksHow qualifying worksThe first round will follow a familiar format, with 12 groups of four or five teams, and the group winners securing World Cup slots. The continent's four remaining berths will then be settled in a 16-team UEFA play-off competition involving the 12 group runners-up and four best-ranked UEFA Nations League section winners who did not finish in the top two of their World Cup qualifying groups.The 16 teams will be drawn into four play-off paths, each featuring four teams, with single-leg semi-finals and finals taking place in March 2026.Top scorers from previous European qualifying campaignsTop scorers from previous European qualifying campaigns1958: Tommy Taylor (England): 8 goals1962: Andrej Kvasnak (Czechoslovakia): 71966: Eusebio (Portugal): 71970: Gerd Muller (West Germany): 91974: Hristo Bonev (Bulgaria), Johan Cruyff (Netherlands), Gigi Riva (Italy), Joachim Streich (East Germany): 71978: Roberto Bettega (Italy): 91982: Karl-Heinz Rummenigge (West Germany): 91986: Preben Ekjaer (Denmark): 81990: Marc van der Linden (Belgium): 71994: Florin Raducioiu (Romania): 91998: Predrag Mijatovic (Yugoslavia): 142002: Andriy Shevchenko (Ukraine): 102006: Pauleta (Portugal): 112010: Theofanis Gekas (Greece): 102014: Robin van Persie (Netherlands): 112018: Robert Lewandowski (Poland): 162022: Harry Kane (England), Memphis Depay (Netherlands): 12FIFA World Cup™ winners from UEFAFIFA World Cup™ winners from UEFAGermany: 4 titles Italy: 4 France: 2 Spain: 1 England: 1
